text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Ivan Peto announced his immediate resignation from the posts of party president and parliamentary group leader of the Free Democrats yesterday. Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze now takes over as president until a special congress. Prime Minister Gyula Horn expressed confidence that the change will not influence coalition co-operation.

- The Central Crime-Fighting Directorate is expected today to recommend that the Capital's Prosecutor's Office bring charges against Marta Tocsik and former leading officials at the State Privatisation and Holding Co.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn told a regular monthly press briefing that the government this year no longer pursues a restrictive policy.
- Before regular business in Parliament yesterday opposition urged an immediate halt to the second stage of the energy privatisation.
- Five companies submitted bids for the prequalification tender for K&H Bank by the Monday afternoon deadline.
- More than 30,000 entirely or partially foreign-owned companies are active in Hungary, Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha told the general meeting of the Joint Venture Association.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Hungary expects to pay back $1 billion of state debts in the form of pre-payment, National Bank of Hungary vice president Gyorgy Szapary told the EBRD annual meeting in London on Monday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Hungarian car manufacturers and importers sold 14,377 cars in the first three months of the year, over 8 percent more than in the same period of last year. The former market leader Opel sold 15 percent less, losing its leading position to Suzuki.
- A total of 4.3 million foreigners visited Hungary in the first two months of this year, 17 percent up on the same period of last year.
- Russians made over one million visits to Hungary last year.
- A total of 85 companies with foreign backing established themselves in Szabolcs-Szatmar-Bereg county last year.
- The operator of the toll section of the M1 motorway is experiencing serious financial problems, spokeswoman Mrs Boros acknowledged yesterday.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- The Industry Ministry projects an annual 5-8 percent growth in building materials production in the next five years.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co yesterday published a list of five companies available for simplified privatisation.
- Shareholders of Shell Hungary Rt appointed a new board of directors and named Shane McNally as managing director.
- Gardenia-1 shares made a successful debut on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Monday as their price rose HUF 300 from the opening HUF 1,465.
